title: Policy-gated browsing preset limited to consent-banner handling and ad/tracker filtering (fingerprint masking deferred to an ADR)
summary: Re-scoped by T2. Keep the benign parts of R-t2-03-11: wire the existing consent-banner script and optional ad/tracker filtering behind an org policy flag, and make locale/timezone/TLS identity consistent with the request context of F-t2-058. Do not wire stealth.rs or fingerprint masking until an ADR on anti-bot posture decides it; F-t2-027 currently recommends deleting the dead stealth code.
whyItMatters: The consolidators disagree: R-t2-04-03 removes stealth code and reports blocks honestly, R-t2-03-11 wires it under policy. Verevon's contract already forbids challenge bypass (ChallengeSignal.requires_escalation defaults to true, SRC), and the honest posture (Codex, SRC) fits Verevon best. Consent handling and ad filtering still save time and cost.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify fingerprint-suite and Camoufox (apify-platform-056 and -057, DOC); Firecrawl behaviorOverrides (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-013, SRC)
others: Firecrawl tlsclient tier with an explicit demotion rule (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-007, SRC) and Apify got-scraping header generation (apify-platform-062, DOC)
Firecrawl blockAds via uBlock Origin Lite on hosted sessions (firecrawl-api-surface-059, SRC)
Codex deliberately ships no stealth because it drives real user browsers (codexbrowser-in-app-browser-011, SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Stealth and TLS identity: 2 of 4 sources (apify, firecrawl), common. Ad blocking: 1 of 4, unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Per session sample a fingerprint {UA, sec-ch-ua, platform, screen, deviceMemory, WebGL vendor/renderer, fonts, locale, timezone} consistent with the egress country; apply it with Emulation.setUserAgentOverride (with userAgentMetadata), setLocaleOverride, setTimezoneOverride, setDeviceMetricsOverride and Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument; persist it with the profile so identity never changes mid-profile; derive HTTP headers from the same profile; planner rule: after a browser attempt fails never demote to a plain client unless explicitly allowed. Ad blocking via an MV3 blocker extension or CDP Fetch.enable with a filter-list matcher.

verevonToday.gap: Stealth and consent scripts are never injected; no fingerprint generator or persisted fingerprint; the planner only picks the Chrome TLS profile; the TLS tier does not follow redirects; the rotator policy is unwired; no ad or tracker blocking.

approach: Ingestion Plane. Phase A (S, hygiene): per-hop-validated redirect following in the TLS driver, planner use of Firefox/Safari profiles, wire FingerprintRotator on block, adopt the no-browser-to-plain-demotion rule. Phase B (M): FingerprintProfile persisted with the browser profile (SessionSnapshot already has UA/locale/timezone fields), applied on context creation; inject default_preamble only under the 'stealth' RunPolicy preset and log it in receipts; derive HTTP headers from the same profile and session locale (depends on R-t2-03-05 emulation). Phase C (S, optional): adblock-rust matcher in the existing CDP Fetch guard plus a default-on consent-dismiss option and a 'block ads' toggle in BrowserChrome. Never apply stealth to customer-owned authenticated SaaS sessions, and do not add CAPTCHA solving as a default (non-goal in the Sovereign Scraping proposal).
dependencies: F-t2-020 (profile persistence to hold the fingerprint)
risks: Terms-of-service and legal exposure on protected sites; arms-race maintenance and fingerprint drift as browsers update; an inconsistent fingerprint is worse than none; filter-list licensing (EasyList is copyleft) and breakage on sites that need ad scripts.

verevon.exactGap: stealth.rs defines STEALTH_SCRIPT, CONSENT_DISMISS_SCRIPT and default_preamble but only its own unit test calls default_preamble (lib.rs:164 merely exports the module), the chromiumoxide launcher sets only crash, shm and QUIC flags with no UA, locale, timezone or addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument call, DriverPlan.stealth_level has no reader, the planner always picks TlsProfile::default(), the TLS adapter deliberately does not follow redirects, and FingerprintRotator::on_block is never called (only is_block_status is used). verevon.constraints: Quarry executes deterministically and records what it did: any Quarry-initiated click such as banner dismissal is not a Model-proposed action and must be logged in receipts and kept off authenticated customer SaaS sessions. Quarry's challenge classifier marks every detected challenge requires_escalation: true (observation.rs:213) rather than bypassing it, which fits F-t2-027's removal of the dead stealth code. ZDR is unaffected. Ad and tracker filtering must live in the existing fail-closed Fetch guard so it cannot weaken the egress policy.
verevon.approachAdjustment: The item contradicts itself: the title defers fingerprint masking to an ADR, but Phase B injects default_preamble (which bundles STEALTH_SCRIPT with the consent script) and builds a persisted FingerprintProfile. Narrow it to: inject CONSENT_DISMISS_SCRIPT alone behind an org policy flag; add an ad and tracker matcher in install_network_guard with a distinct receipt decision; per-hop validated redirect following in the TLS driver; locale and timezone from the session context (F-t2-058). Also change the consent script's behaviour: it deliberately clicks the affirmative accept button (stealth.rs:290-291) and so grants tracking consent on the user's behalf, which is the wrong default for a Norwegian and EU product; prefer reject-all or necessary-only controls, or hide the overlay, and record the choice. Move FingerprintProfile persistence and FingerprintRotator wiring under the anti-bot ADR.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged in size after narrowing: consent injection and TLS redirect hygiene are S each, the ad and tracker matcher with filter-list licensing is M; the dropped fingerprint profile work would have been the larger part.
verevon.verdictReason: Confirmed stub with no production path, but the proposed wiring (default_preamble, FingerprintProfile) exceeds the item's own stated scope and the existing consent script accepts cookies instead of rejecting them; reword to the consent, filter and redirect-hygiene scope.
